title: Combined effects of guanidinoacetic acid, coenzyme Q10 and taurine on growth performance, gene expression and ascites mortality in broiler chickens.

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>High levels of guanidinoacetate acid (GAA) deteriorate growth response in broiler chickens. We propose using coenzyme Q<jats:sub>10</jats:sub>, an antioxidant, and taurine (TAU), a methyl donor, to cope with the situation when high level of GAA included in diet. GAA was supplemented at 0 (control), 0.75, 1.5 and 2.25 g/kg in isoenergetic and isonitrogenous diets and fed to broilers (Cobb 500) from 1 to 40 days post‐hatch. Three additional diets were prepared by adding CoQ<jats:sub>10</jats:sub> (40 mg/kg), TAU (40 mg/kg) or their combination (both CoQ<jats:sub>10</jats:sub> and TAU at 40 mg/kg) to the 2.25 g/kg GAA group. The experimental design used was a completely randomized design. While weight gain (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> = 0.038) and feed conversion ratio (<jats:italic>p = </jats:italic>0.024) improved when GAA added at 1.5 g/kg, higher supplementation (2.25 g/kg) deteriorated these responses. These responses, however, were significantly restored by using CoQ<jats:sub>10</jats:sub>, TAU or their combination. Abdominal fat deposition was significantly decreased when TAU added to broiler diets by virtue of upregulating peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor alpha. Supplementing broiler diets with CoQ<jats:sub>10</jats:sub> and TAU or their combination significantly decrease ascites mortality. In conclusion, CoQ<jats:sub>10</jats:sub> and TAU have shown beneficial effects when high level of GAA included in broiler diets.</jats:p>
